definitions.leaker: a of the leak event, parsed from event_id '<t0>_leak_<a>'; checked against column a of every released table row read
definitions.repeat: the leaker is the a of at least one completed earlier library event: its onset + 7200 s <= this event's onset (history definition). Development definition: the same, counting only library events with onset before the test period
definitions.library: successful (error null) leak events with t0_obs of the released event tables; R1: 2023-2025; R2: 2023-2026 (2026 table ends 2026-08-31) plus the scored R2 events (onset from the R2 rows)
definitions.contrast_statistic: event-macro mean AP difference over the class's eligible events, then the training-seed mean (published estimand restricted to the class)
definitions.intervals: day_blocks: training seeds then incident-day blocks rebuilt from the class's events (paired_bootstrap); leaker_x_day: paper_actor_bootstrap.two_way_bootstrap; repeat_minus_first_seen: one joint draw for both classes (blocks or leakers and days of all eligible events)

R2.history_gap: R2 identified 1,311 events (sections/08-forecast.tex); the 1,289 scored ones are local. The other 22 (onset outside the window) and their leakers are held only in the custodian event table, so a leaker whose only completed earlier event is one of them is classed first-seen here. The released 2026 table covers 1 January to 31 August 2026.
R2.same_leaker_baseline: not computed: R2 records name only the seeds, not the target or new members

same_leaker_baseline_scope.candidates: native candidates of online history (all ASes with positive participation in the available library, plus the seeds); the shared (graph) candidate identities are held only in the graph files, not in the per-event records, so the shared-candidate variant is not computed
same_leaker_baseline_scope.availability: library events with onset + 7200 s <= issue time (onset + Delta), as the history arm; the repeat class uses onset + 7200 s <= onset
same_leaker_baseline_scope.ties: exact expectation over random orders within ties (event_ranking_metrics)
same_leaker_baseline_scope.input_gap: the released seed sets count ASes by raw first-seen time, the forecast input by availability; on events with gap k > 0 the released set holds k ASes that were not yet input seeds, which cannot be identified from the released files (see the module docstring)

populations.released_inputs: published eligible events with a new member under the released seed sets; all three rankings on the released seed sets; no SAGE contrast
populations.exact_inputs: published eligible events with k = 0, where the reconstruction equals the published online history native record per event; SAGE contrasts here
